home: Welcome to Bharata, an atlas of the Indian subcontinent from the year 600 to 1700. Scroll down to fall from orbit onto the map, and watch kingdoms rise and fade across eleven centuries. Every claim names its source, and where we do not know, the atlas says so.
atlas: This is the atlas. Drag the timeline at the bottom to move through the years, and watch borders change. Click a kingdom to see its rulers, its capitals and its battles. Press the question mark for keyboard shortcuts, or play the timeline to see history unfold on its own.
chronology: This is the timeline. Each coloured lane is one kingdom, drawn from its first year to its last, so you can see at a glance who ruled at the same time. Battles are marked along the bottom. Click any lane to open that kingdom.
polities: These are the kingdoms, empires and sultanates of the atlas. Move the slider to see which of them held land in any given year, or search by name. Each card opens a page with its rulers, places, events and evidence.
people: These are the rulers recorded in the atlas, grouped by kingdom and sorted by their dates. Some dates describe a reign and some only a lifetime, and the page says which. Search by name, or jump straight to a kingdom.
places: These are the places of the atlas: capitals, temples, forts, tombs and mosques, each with a position on the map. Some are protected monuments today, and the page says so. Choose a place to see which kingdoms held it, and when.
evidence: This is the evidence room. Here you can read real translations of inscriptions, and follow each claim back to its source. The page shows what is certain, what is uncertain, and why, so you can judge for yourself.
search: This is the search page. Choose rulers, kingdoms, places or events, then narrow them with filters. You can ask for rulers who reigned during a battle, kingdoms that shared a border, or places inside a kingdom in a particular year.
data: This is the database browser. Every table behind the atlas is open here, from kingdoms and rulers to sources and images. Choose a table to read its rows exactly as they are stored.
connections: This diagram shows how the tables of the database are linked. Each box is a table, and each line is a connection, for example a ruler belonging to a kingdom, or a battle taking place inside one. Use it to understand how the records fit together.
polities-ahmadnagar: Ahmadnagar Sultanate. A sultanate in Deccan, from around 1492 to around 1652. The Ahmadnagar Sultanate was a medieval Deccani Muslim kingdom located in the northwestern Deccan, between the sultanates of Gujarat and Bijapur, ruled by the Nizam Shahi dynasty. It was established by Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I in 1490. Its capital was Ahilyanagar.
polities-anuradhapura: Anuradhapura Kingdom. A kingdom in Sri Lanka, from around 439 to around 1017. The Kingdom of Anuradhapura, named for its capital city, was the second established Sinhalese kingdom of ancient Sri Lanka. According to the Mahāvaṃsa, it was founded by King Pandukabhaya in 437 BC, whose authority extended throughout the country.
polities-bahmani: Bahmani. A sultanate in Northern Deccan, from 1347 to 1527. Founded in 1347 when Deccan nobles revolted against Delhi and made Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah their king at Gulbarga. The capital moved to Bidar in 1429. Its capitals were Gulbarga and Bidar. The atlas records 23 rulers.
polities-bengal-sultanate: Bengal Sultanate. A sultanate in Bengal, from around 1344 to around 1533. The Bengal Sultanate was a late medieval sultanate based in the Bengal region in eastern South Asia between the 14th and 16th centuries. It was the dominant power of the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, with a network of mint towns spread across the region.
polities-berar: Berar Sultanate. A sultanate in Central India, from around 1492 to around 1578. The Berar Sultanate was an early modern Indian kingdom in the Deccan, ruled by the Imad Shahi dynasty. It was one of the Deccan sultanates, and was established in 1490 following the disintegration of the Bahmani Sultanate by Fathullah Imad-ul-Mulk.
polities-bidar-sultanate: Bidar Sultanate. A sultanate in Deccan, from around 1492 to around 1618. The Sultanate of Bidar was an early modern Indian polity, ruled by the Barid Shahi dynasty that ruled a territory in the central Deccan centred at Bidar.
polities-bijapur: Bijapur Sultanate. A sultanate in Deccan, from around 1492 to around 1686. The Sultanate of Bijapur was an early modern kingdom in the western Deccan and South India, ruled by the Muslim Adil Shahi dynasty.
polities-chalukya-badami: Chalukya. A kingdom in Deccan, from 543 to 753. The Chalukya dynasty was a Classical Indian dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and the 12th centuries. During this period, they ruled as three related yet individual dynasties. Its capital was Badami. The atlas records 13 rulers.
polities-chalukya-kalyani: Chalukya. An empire in Deccan, from 973 to 1189. The Chalukyas of Kalyani, who overthrew the Rashtrakutas in 973 and ruled the western Deccan for two centuries. Under Vikramaditya VI, inscriptions counted the years from 1076, when he became king. Its capital was Basavakalyan. The atlas records 12 rulers.
polities-chandela: Chandela. A kingdom in Gangetic plain, from around 960 to around 1313. The Chandelas of Jejakabhukti was an Indian dynasty in Central India. The Chandelas ruled much of the Bundelkhand region between the 9th and the 13th centuries. Its capital was Khajuraho. The atlas records 17 rulers.
polities-chandra: Chandra. A kingdom in Bengal, from around 900 to around 1055. The Chandra dynasty was a Buddhist dynasty, originating from the South-east Bengal region of Indian subcontinent, which ruled the Samatata area of Bengal, as well as parts of Arakan Later it was a neighbour to the Pala Empire to the north.
polities-chauhan: Chauhan. A kingdom in Rajasthan, from around 980 to around 1201. The Chauhan dynasty are a dynasty associated with various ruling Rajput families in the present-day Indian state of Rajasthan from seventh century onwards. Its capital was Delhi. The atlas records 19 rulers.
polities-chaulukya: Chaulukya. A kingdom in Gujarat and Malwa, from around 947 to around 1249. The Chaulukya dynasty, also Solanki dynasty, was a dynasty that ruled parts of what are now Gujarat and Rajasthan in north-western India, between c. 940 CE and c. The atlas records 12 rulers.
polities-chera: Chera. A kingdom in Southern India, from around 844 to around 1124. Kings of the Kerala coast, known in this period as the Chera Perumals, who ruled from Kodungallur. Their ports sent pepper and other spices across the Indian Ocean to the Middle East. Its capital was Kodungallur. The atlas records 11 rulers.
polities-chola: Chola. An empire in Southern India, from around 850 to 1279. A Tamil dynasty from the Kaveri delta. Under Rajaraja I and his son Rajendra I it ruled most of southern India and northern Sri Lanka, and its fleets crossed the Bay of Bengal. Its capitals were Thanjavur and Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
polities-dambadeniya: Dambadeniya. A kingdom in Sri Lanka, from around 1236 to around 1293. The Kingdom of Dambadeniya was a medieval Sinhalese kingdom in what is present-day Sri Lanka. The kingdom's rulers reigned from 1220–1345. Its capital was Dambadeniya. The atlas records 4 rulers.
polities-delhi-sultanate: Delhi Sultanate. A sultanate in Northern India, from 1206 to 1526. The state that began in 1206, when Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a general of Muhammad of Ghor, became ruler of his master's conquests in India.
polities-eastern-ganga: Eastern Ganga. A kingdom in Odisha and the east coast, from 1078 to 1434. The Eastern Ganga dynasty were a large medieval era dynasty that reigned from Kalinga from as early as the 5th century to the mid 20th century.
polities-gahadavala: Gahadavala. A kingdom in Gangetic plain, from around 1085 to around 1201. The Gahadavala dynasty, also known as Gahadavalas of Kannauj, was a Rajput dynasty that ruled parts of the present-day Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, during 11th and 12th centuries.
polities-ghaznavid: Ghaznavid. A kingdom in Afghanistan and northern India, from around 962 to around 1209. The Ghaznavid Empire was a culturally Persianate, Sunni Muslim state flourishing from 977 to 1186. The empire spread from the Oxus to the Indus Valley at its greatest extent. Its capital was Lahore. The atlas records 24 rulers.
polities-ghurid: Ghurid. A kingdom in Afghanistan and northern India, from around 1152 to around 1209. The Ghurid dynasty was a culturally Persianate dynasty of eastern Iranian Tajik origin, which ruled from the 8th-century in the region of Ghor, and became an Empire from 1175 to 1215.
polities-golconda: Golconda Sultanate. A sultanate in Deccan, from around 1519 to around 1686. The Sultanate of Golconda was an early modern kingdom in southern India, ruled by the Persianate, Shia Islamic Qutb Shahi dynasty of Turkoman origin.
polities-gorkha: Gorkha Kingdom. A kingdom in Himalaya and Nepal, from around 1588 to around 1717. The Gorkha Kingdom, also known as the Gorkha Confederation or the Gorkha Empire, was one of the 24 Khasa principally state or Chaubisi states, situated at the junction of the Himalayas and the Indian subcontinent.
polities-habbarid: Habbarid Emirate of Sind. An emirate in Afghanistan and Sindh, from around 860 to around 1201. The Habbari Dynasty were an Arab dynasty that ruled much of Sindh, as a semi-independent emirate from 854 to 1024.
polities-harsha: Harsha's Empire. An empire in Northern India, from around 612 to around 655. Harshavardhana was the emperor of Kannauj from April 606 until his death in 647. He was the king of Thanesar who had defeated the Alchon Huns, and the younger brother of Rajyavardhana, son of Prabhakaravardhana and last king of Thanesar.
polities-hoysala: Hoysala. A kingdom in Deccan, from around 1026 to 1343. A southern Karnataka kingdom known above all for its intricately carved soapstone temples — the Chennakeshava Temple at Belur and Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu remain among the most ornamented in India. Its capitals were Dorasamudra and Belur. The atlas records 13 rulers.
polities-jaffna: Jaffna. A kingdom in Sri Lanka, from around 1314 to around 1594. The Jaffna Kingdom, also known as Kingdom of Aryachakravarti, was a historical kingdom of what today is northern Sri Lanka.
polities-jaunpur: Jaunpur Sultanate. A sultanate in Gangetic plain, from around 1395 to around 1481. The Jaunpur Sultanate was a late medieval Indian Muslim state which ruled over much of what is now the Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar and southern Nepal between 1394 and 1494.
polities-kakatiya: Kakatiya. A kingdom in Deccan, from 1163 to 1323. The Kakatiya dynasty was a Telugu dynasty that ruled most of eastern Deccan region in present-day India between 12th and 14th centuries. Their territory comprised much of the present day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, parts of eastern Karnataka, northern Tamil Nadu, and southern Odisha.
polities-kamarupa: Kamarupa. A kingdom in Assam and the north-east, from around 555 to around 1138. Kamarupa, an early state during the Classical period on the Indian subcontinent, was the first historical kingdom of Assam. The Kamrupa word first appeared in the Samudragupta Allahabad Edict before that there is no mention of existence of this word.
polities-kampili: Kampili. A kingdom in Karnataka and the Deccan, from around 1285 to around 1332. The Kampili kingdom was a short-lived Hindu kingdom in the 14th century CE in South India. The kingdom existed near Ballari in the Tungabhadra river in the northeastern parts of the present-day Karnataka state, India. Its capital was Kammatadurga.
polities-karkota: Karkota. A kingdom in Kashmir and the Himalaya, from around 592 to around 859. The Karkota dynasty ruled over the Kashmir valley and some northern parts of the Indian subcontinent during 7th and 8th centuries.
polities-kashmir-sultanate: Kashmir Sultanate. A sultanate in Kashmir and the Himalaya, from around 1344 to around 1587. The Kashmir Sultanate, historically Latinised as the Sultanate of Cashmere, was a medieval kingdom primarily based in the Kashmir Valley, in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, between the early 14th and late 16th centuries.
polities-lohara: Lohara. A kingdom in Kashmir and the Himalaya, from around 1003 to around 1259. The Lohar dynasty was a dynasty that ruled over Kashmir and surrounding regions in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent between 1003 and approximately 1175.
polities-madurai-nayaks: Madurai Nayaks. A kingdom in Southern India, from around 1529 to around 1712. The Madurai Nayaks were a Telugu-speaking dynasty of Balija origin that ruled large parts of modern-day Tamil Nadu, India, between the 16th and 18th centuries, with Madurai as their capital.
polities-maitraka: Maitraka. A kingdom in Gujarat and Malwa, from around 555 to around 731. The Maitraka dynasty ruled the Kingdom of Valabhi in western India from approximately 475 to 776 from their capital at Vallabhi. With the sole exception of Dharapaṭṭa, who is associated with sun-worship, they were followers of Shaivism. Its capital was Vallabhi.
polities-maratha: Maratha Empire. An empire in Deccan, from 1674 to 1818. The Maratha Empire, also referred to as the Maratha Confederacy, was an early modern polity in the Indian subcontinent.
polities-mughal: Mughal Empire. An empire in Northern India and the Deccan, from around 1529 to around 1705. The Mughal Empire was an early modern empire in South Asia.
polities-mysore: Kingdom of Mysore. A kingdom in Karnataka and the Deccan, from around 1572 to around 1708. The Kingdom of Mysore was a geopolitical realm in southern India founded in around 1399 in the vicinity of the modern-day city of Mysuru.
polities-pala: Pala. An empire in Bengal and Bihar, from around 750 to around 1161. A dynasty from Bengal that began, by tradition, with the election of Gopala as king around 750. Under Dharmapala and Devapala it ruled Bengal and Bihar and fought the Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas for control of Kannauj.
polities-pallava: Pallava. A kingdom in Tamil country and Andhra, from around 275 to 897. The Pallava dynasty ruled from 275 to 897 in southern India, including a significant portion of the Deccan and Tondaimandalam. The dynasty rose to prominence after the downfall of the Satavahana Empire, whom they had formerly served as feudatories.
polities-pandya: Pandya. A kingdom in Southern India, from around 590 to around 1345. One of the oldest Tamil dynasties, ruling from Madurai. In the 1250s, under Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I, it expanded north into the Telugu country and conquered northern Sri Lanka, until the Delhi Sultanate's invasion of 1310–11. Its capital was Madurai.
polities-paramara: Paramara. A kingdom in Malwa, from around 980 to around 1235. The Paramara dynasty was an Indian dynasty that ruled Malwa and surrounding areas in west-central India between 948 and 1305. They belonged to the Paramara clan of the Rajputs. The atlas records 15 rulers.
polities-polonnaruwa: Polonnaruwa. A kingdom in Sri Lanka, from around 1072 to around 1259. The Kingdom of Polonnaruwa was the Sinhalese kingdom that expanded across the island of Sri Lanka from 1070 until 1232. The kingdom unified the island and started expanding its overseas influence during the reign of Parakramabahu the Great. Its capital was Polonnaruwa.
polities-pratihara: Gurjara-Pratihara. An empire in Northern and western India, from around 730 to 1036. A dynasty that rose in Malwa and Rajasthan in the 8th century and secured the throne of Kannauj in 816, which became the centre of its state.
polities-rashtrakuta: Rashtrakuta. An empire in Deccan, from 753 to 982. A Deccan dynasty that took power from the Chalukyas of Badami around 753.
polities-samma: Samma. A kingdom in Sindh and Makran, from around 1344 to around 1525. The Samma dynasty was a medieval Sindhi Muslim dynasty based in Sindh. It was established by Unar bin Babinah in 1351 after defeating Hamir and declaring independence from the Delhi Sultanate. Its capital was Thatta. The atlas records 19 rulers.
polities-sena: Sena. A kingdom in Bengal, from around 1072 to around 1235. The Sena dynasty, or the Senas, were a Hindu dynasty that succeeded the Pala Empire and ruled much of the eastern region of the Indian subcontinent from Bengal, during the early medieval period, through the 11th and 13th centuries. Its capital was Nabadwip.
polities-sur: Sur Empire. An empire in Northern India, from around 1540 to around 1594. The Sur Empire was an empire ruled by the Afghan-origin Sur dynasty in northern India for nearly 16 or 18 years, between 1538/1540 and 1556, with Sasaram serving as its capital. It was founded by Sher Shah Suri.
polities-thanjavur-marathas: Thanjavur Marathas. A kingdom in Southern India, from around 1677 to around 1712. The Thanjavur Maratha kingdom, ruled by the Bhonsle dynasty, was a South Indian Monarchy that governed the Kaveri delta from 1675 to 1855. It was established by Maratha general Ekoji I, with its capital at Thanjavur. Its capital was Thanjavur.
polities-thanjavur-nayaks: Thanjavur Nayaks. A kingdom in Southern India, from around 1534 to around 1676. The Thanjavur Nayak Dynasty, established by Sevappa Nayaka around 1532, was a ruling lineage that governed Thanjavur between 16th and 17th centuries.
polities-turk-shahis: Turk Shahis. A kingdom in Afghanistan and Sindh, from around 561 to around 874. The Turk Shahis were a dynasty of Western Turk, or mixed Turco-Hephthalite origin, that ruled from Kabul and Kapisa to Gandhara in the 7th to 9th centuries CE. They may have been of Khalaj ethnicity. Its capital was Kabul.
polities-utpala: Utpala. A kingdom in Kashmir and the Himalaya, from around 960 to around 1002. The Utpala Dynasty was a medieval Kashmiri Hindu dynasty that ruled over Kashmir from the 9th to 10th centuries. Founded by Avantivarman in 855, it replaced the Karkota dynasty. Its capital was Awantipora. The atlas records 5 rulers.
polities-vijayanagara: Vijayanagara. An empire in Deccan / Southern India, from 1336 to 1646. An empire founded in 1336 and ruled from the city of Vijayanagara, today's Hampi. It was at its largest under Krishnadevaraya in the early 1500s. Its capitals were Hampi and Penukonda and Chandragiri. The atlas records 31 rulers.
polities-yadava: Yadava. A kingdom in Deccan, from around 1188 to around 1325. The Seuna, Sevuna, or Yadavas of Devagiri was a medieval Indian dynasty, which at its peak ruled a realm stretching from the Narmada river in the north to the Tungabhadra river in the south, in the western part of the Deccan region.
people-abd-al-rashid-ben-mahmud: Abd al-Rashid ben Mahmud, Sultan of the Ghaznavid Empire. Ruled around 1049 to around 1052. Not much more is recorded here yet. Ghaznavid is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abdullah-1626-golconda: Abdullah, Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda. Ruled around 1626 to around 1672. Abdullah Qutb Shah was the seventh ruler of the kingdom of Golconda in southern India under the Qutb Shahi dynasty. He ruled from 1626 to 1672. Golconda Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abdullah-ibn-umar-884-habbarid: Abdullah ibn Umar, Habbarid emir of Mansura. Ruled around 884 to around 913. Not much more is recorded here yet. Habbarid Emirate of Sind is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abhimanyu-ii-958-utpala: Abhimanyu the Second, King of Kashmir. Ruled around 958 to around 972. Not much more is recorded here yet. Utpala (Kashmir) is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abhinavaditya-645-chalukya-badami: Abhinavaditya, Chalukya Emperor from 645 to 646. Ruled around 645 to around 646. Abhinavaditya (r. c. Chalukya (Badami) is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abu-bakr-shah-1389-delhi-sultanat: Abu Bakr Shah, Sultan of Delhi. Ruled around 1389 to around 1390. Abu Bakr Shah Tughlaq was a Muslim ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty. He was the son of Zafar Khan and the grandson of Sultan Feroze Shah Tughluq. Delhi Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-abul-hasan-1672-golconda: Abul Hasan, Qutb Shahi Sultan of Golconda. Ruled around 1672 to around 1687. Abul Hasan Qutb Shah, also known as Abul Hasan Tana Shah, was the eighth and last ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, sovereign of the Kingdom of Golconda in South India. He ruled from 1672 to 1686.
people-achuthappa-nayaka-1560-thanjavur-: Achuthappa Nayaka, Nayak ruler of Thanjavur. Ruled around 1560 to around 1614. Achuthappa Nayak was the Nayaka of Thanjavur under the Vijayanagara Empire from 1560 to 1614. From 1560 to 1580, he was co-Nayaka along with his father and from 1580 to 1614, he ruled on his own.
people-achyuta-deva-raya-1529-vijayanaga: Achyuta Deva Raya, Emperor of Vijayanagara. Ruled around 1529 to around 1542. Achyuta Deva Raya (died June 1542) was a emperor of Vijayanagara who succeeded his older brother, Krishnadevaraya, after the latter's death in 1529. Vijayanagara is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-adil-shah-suri-1555-sur: Adil Shah Suri, Sur Sultan. Ruled around 1555 to around 1556. Muhammad Adil Shah (Muhammad Mubariz Khan; died 1557) was Sultan of the Sur Empire from December 1554 until his defeat in January 1555. He was the last Suri ruler of the united empire, after which the empire fell into civil war.
people-aditya-i: Aditya the First, Chola king. Ruled around 871 to around 907. Aditya Chola I was a Chola king who reigned in the late ninth to early tenth century CE.
people-adityavarman-643-chalukya-badami: Adityavarman, Chalukya Emperor from 643 to 645. Ruled around 643 to around 645. Adityavarma (r. c. Chalukya (Badami) is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-aggabodhi-i-571-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the First, King of Anuradhapura. Lived around 571 to around 604. Aggabodhi I (also known as Akbo) was a king of the Anuradhapura Kingdom in the 6th and 7th centuries.
people-aggabodhi-ii-598-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Second, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 598 to around 608. Aggabodhi II, (r. 604–614 CE or 608–618 CE), also known as Kuda Akbo, was a monarch of the Anuradhapura Kingdom in modern-day Sri Lanka. Anuradhapura Kingdom is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-aggabodhi-iii-623-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Third, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 623. Aggabodhi III, also known as Sirisangabo, was a monarch of the Anuradhapura Kingdom who reigned during a period of extreme political instability in the 7th century.
people-aggabodhi-iii-second-term-624-anu: Aggabodhi the Third, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 624 to around 640. Not much more is recorded here yet. Anuradhapura Kingdom is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-aggabodhi-iv-673-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Fourth, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 673 to around 689. Aggabodhi IV was King of Anuradhapura in the 7th century, whose reign lasted from 673 to 689(667 to 683). Anuradhapura Kingdom is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-aggabodhi-ix-843-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Ninth, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 843 to around 846. Aggabodhi IX was King of Anuradhapura in the 9th century, whose reign lasted from 843 to 846. He succeeded his father Dappula III as King of Anuradhapura and was succeeded by his brother Sena I.
people-aggabodhi-v-726-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Fifth, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 726 to around 732. Aggabodhi V was King of Anuradhapura in the 8th century, whose reign lasted from 726 to 732. He succeeded his father Manavanna as King of Anuradhapura and was succeeded by his brother Kassapa III.
people-aggabodhi-vi-741-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Sixth, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 741 to around 781. Aggabodhi VI was King of Anuradhapura in the 8th century, whose reign lasted from 741 to 781. He succeeded his uncle Mahinda I as King of Anuradhapura and was succeeded by his cousin Aggabodhi VII.
people-aggabodhi-vii-781-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Seventh, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 781 to around 787. Aggabodhi VI was King of Anuradhapura in the 8th century, whose reign lasted from 741 to 781. He succeeded his uncle Mahinda I as King of Anuradhapura and was succeeded by his cousin Aggabodhi VII.
people-aggabodhi-viii-816-anuradhapura: Aggabodhi the Eighth, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 816 to around 827. Aggabodhi VIII was King of Anuradhapura in the 9th century, whose reign lasted from 816 to 827. He succeeded his brother Mahinda III as King of Anuradhapura and was succeeded by his brother Dappula III.
people-ahmad-nizam-shah-i-1490-ahmadnaga: Ahmad Nizam Shah the First, Nizam Shahi Sultan of Ahmadnagar. Ruled around 1490 to around 1510. Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah was the founder of the Nizam Shahi dynasty and the Ahmadnagar Sultanate. Ahmadnagar Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-ahmad-shah-i-wali-1422-bahmani: Ahmad Shah I Wali, Sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate from 1422 to 1436. Ruled around 1422 to around 1436. Shihab-ud-Din Ahmad Shah I Bahmani, also known as Ahmad Shah Wali (lit.
people-ahmed-shah-bahmani-ii-1518-bahman: Ahmed Shah Bahmani the Second, Bahmani Sultan. Ruled around 1518 to around 1520. Not much more is recorded here yet. Bahmani is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-ahmed-shah-wali-bahmani-1422-bahm: Ahmed Shah Wali Bahmani, Bahmani Sultan. Ruled around 1422 to around 1436. Shihab-ud-Din Ahmad Shah I Bahmani, also known as Ahmad Shah Wali, was the Sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate from 1 October 1422 to 17 April 1436, and was a great patron of arts and culture.
people-ajayapala-1171-chaulukya: Ajayapala, Chaulukya king of Gujarat. Ruled around 1171 to around 1175. Ajayapala (reigned c. 1171–1175) was an Indian king from the Chaulukya (Solanki) dynasty of Gujarat. Chaulukya (Solanki) is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-ajaya-raja-ii-1110-chauhan: Ajaya-raja the Second, Chahamana king of Shakambhari. Ruled around 1110 to around 1135. Not much more is recorded here yet. Chauhan is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-akbar: Akbar, Mughal emperor. Ruled around 1556 to around 1605. Akbar, also known as Akbar the Great, was the third Mughal emperor, who reigned from 1556 to 1605. Akbar succeeded his father, Humayun, under a regent, Bairam Khan, who helped the young emperor expand and consolidate Mughal domains in the Indian subcontinent.
people-ala-al-din-husayn-1149-ghurid: Ala al-Din Husayn, Ghurid ruler. Ruled around 1149 to around 1161. Ala al-Din Husayn was king of the Ghurid dynasty from 1149 to 1161. He was one of the greatest Ghurid kings, and it was during his reign that the Ghurid dynasty rose to prominence. Ghurid is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-aladdin-imad-shah-1504-berar: Aladdin Imad Shah, Imad Shahi Sultan of Berar. Ruled around 1504 to around 1529. Aladdin Imad Shah was the second Sultan of Berar. He reigned between 1504 and 1529. Berar Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-alagiri-nayak-1675-madurai-nayaks: Alagiri Nayak, Ruler of Madurai Nayaks. Ruled around 1675 to around 1690. Alagiri Nayak was the younger brother of the Madurai Nayak king Chokkanatha Nayak and the last Nayak king of Thanjavur. In 1675, Thanjavur was conquered by Ekoji I, the half-brother of Shivaji who founded the Thanjavur Maratha kingdom.
people-alam-shah-1445-delhi-sultanate: Alam Shah, Sultan of Delhi. Ruled around 1445 to around 1451. Ala-ud-Din Alam Shah was the fourth and last ruler of the Sayyid dynasty which ruled the Delhi Sultanate. people-satyashraya-997-chalukya-kalyani: Satyashraya, Western Chalukya Emperor from 997 to 1008. Ruled around 997 to around 1008. Satyashraya (IAST: Satyāśraya; died 1008), also known as Sattiga or Irivabedanga, was a king of the Western Chalukya Empire.

people-shurapala-i-854-pala: Shurapala the First, Pala Emperor. Ruled around 854 to around 866. Shurapala I (also spelt Surapala) was a 9th-century ruler of the Pala Empire, in the Bengal region of the Indian subcontinent. He was the fifth Pala emperor. Pala is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.

people-sikandar-khan-lodi-1489-delhi-sul: Sikandar Khan Lodi, Sultan of Delhi. Ruled around 1489 to around 1517. people-sikandar-shah-1358-bengal-sultana: Sikandar Shah, Sultan of Bengal. Ruled around 1358 to around 1390. people-silakala-ambasamanera-518-anuradh: Silakala Ambasamanera, King of Anuradhapura. Ruled around 518 to around 531. Silakala, (reigned c. 518 – 531 CE) was a monarch of the Anuradhapura Kingdom in Sri Lanka. Anuradhapura Kingdom is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.

Sena is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-viswanatha-nayak-1529-madurai-nay: Viswanatha Nayak, Nayak ruler of Madurai. Ruled around 1529 to around 1563. Viswanatha Nayaka (died 1564) was the Vijayanagara viceroy to Madurai in south India and later the ruler of Madurai from 1529 to 1564. He is the founder of the Nayak dynasty of Madurai. Madurai Nayaks is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-vitukathazhakiya-perumal-1103-che: Vitukathazhakiya Perumal, Satiyaputra Chera ruler of Thagadur. Ruled around 1103 to around 1123. Rajarajadevan Vitukathazhakiya Perumal (fl. late 12th century AD), also known as Vyamukta Sravanojjvala in Sanskrit, was an Adigaman Chera ruler of Thagadur (modern Dharmapuri) in northern Tamil Nadu, southern India under Chola monarch Kulothunga III.
people-vuppadeva-1172-lohara: Vuppadeva, King of Kashmir. Ruled around 1172 to around 1181. Not much more is recorded here yet. Lohara (Kashmir) is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-waliullah-shah-bahmani-1522-bahma: Waliullah Shah Bahmani, Bahmani Sultan. Ruled around 1522 to around 1526. Not much more is recorded here yet. Bahmani is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-yakub-shah-chak-1586-kashmir-sult: Yakub Shah Chak, Sultan of Kashmir from 1586 to 1589. Ruled around 1586 to around 1589. Ya'qūb (Yākūb) Shāh Chak was the sixth and the last Chak Sultan of Kashmir Sultanate, who reigned from 1586 to 1589.
people-yashovarman-1133-paramara: Yashovarman, Paramara king of Malwa. Ruled around 1133 to around 1142. Yashovarman (IAST: Yaśovarman; reigned 1133–1142) was an Indian king from the Paramara dynasty, who ruled in the Malwa region of central India.
people-yasho-varman-ii-1164-chandela: Yasho-Varman the Second, Chandela king. Ruled around 1164 to around 1165. Not much more is recorded here yet. Chandela is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-yousuf-shah-1578-kashmir-sultanat: Yousuf Shah, Sultan of Kashmir. Ruled around 1578 to around 1579. Nasir al-Din Muhammad Yusuf Shah, better known as Yousuf Shah Chak was the fourth Sultan of Kashmir from the Chak dynasty from 1578 to 1579 and then from 1580 to 1586.
people-yusuf-adil-shah-1490-bijapur: Yusuf Adil Shah, Adil Shahi Sultan of Bijapur. Ruled around 1490 to around 1510. Yusuf Adil Shah, referred as Yusuf Adil Khan or Hidalcão by the Portuguese, was the founder of the Adil Shahi dynasty that ruled the Sultanate of Bijapur for nearly two centuries.
people-zafar-khan-1299-delhi-sultanate: Zafar Khan, Ruler of Delhi Sultanate. Lived around 1299. Hizabruddin, better known by his title Zafar Khan, was a general of the Delhi Sultanate ruler Alauddin Khalji. He held charge of Multan, Samana, and Sivistan at various times during Alauddin's reign. Delhi Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
people-zayn-al-abidin-1418-kashmir-sulta: Zayn al-Abidin, Sultan of Kashmir. Ruled around 1418 to around 1419. Qutb al-Din Zayn al-Abidin, more famously known as Zayn al-Abidin the Great, was the ninth sultan of the Kashmir Sultanate.
people-zayn-al-abidin-second-term-1420-k: Zayn al-Abidin, Sultan of Kashmir. Ruled around 1420 to around 1470. Not much more is recorded here yet. Kashmir Sultanate is one of the kingdoms in this atlas.
